tags.chapter_name: Center of Mass Momentum and Collision

question.text: A block of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> is at rest at the edge of a table, of height 1 m. A bullet of mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math> collides with the block and sticks to it. If the velocity of the bullet is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> in the horizontal direction just before the collision then the kinetic energy just before the combined system strikes the floor, is [Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi><mo> </mo><mo>=</mo><mo> </mo><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></math>. Assume there is no rotational motion and loss of energy after the collision is negligible.]

solution.text:
Conservation of linear momentum

0.1×20=0.1+1.9×v

v=1 m s-1

Using work energy theorem

Wg=∆k

2×g×1=k-12×2×12

∴   k=21 J
